function.description: route.advance@1.0.0: Advance one evidence-led action. build constructs and validates only: no solve, score or trajectory. run executes a saved build and evaluates its saved result (one charged backend attempt). optimize searches within variables[path]=[lower_bound, upper_bound], executing and evaluating candidates (up to max_trials charged attempts); bounds are not sample values. diagnose analyzes saved results; crosscheck independently executes the same physical/control configuration on an authorized alternative backend (one charged attempt); video renders saved results; finish delivers a valid evaluation, including an unmet task tolerance. Only run, optimize and crosscheck consume solver budget. source_node and changes semantics are specified in the input schema. Cite previous node result evidence after the first action.

action.description: build constructs only; run simulates and evaluates a saved build; optimize searches and evaluates; diagnose analyzes saved results; crosscheck executes independently; video renders saved results; finish delivers an evaluated candidate.
action.title: Action

candidate_id.description: Optional candidate label on build; selects an optimization trial on later actions, defaulting to its best valid trial. A single run preserves the build candidate label.
candidate_id.title: Candidate Id

changes.description: build/optimize only: edits from the declared space, including template, physical paths, discretization paths and control/ paths. Applied to the source configuration, or the frozen baseline when no source is supplied.
changes.title: Changes

combination.description: Authorized combination name. Required for build, optimize without source_node, and crosscheck. With an optimization source, omit to preserve its bindings; an explicit choice must match them.
combination.title: Combination

evidence.description: After the first action, cite at least one previous route node result reference here. route overview already supplies these references; a separate read is optional.
evidence.title: Evidence

max_trials.description: Maximum optimizer proposals, bounded by route max_trials; independent of single run, which needs one solve. Duplicate proposals may reuse saved results.
max_trials.title: Max Trials

next_step.description: English statement of the intended next decision or stopping condition.
next_step.title: Next Step

node_id.description: Unique label for this route action; reuse the original request_id to recover a sealed call.
node_id.title: Node Id

reason.description: English explanation grounded in the current overview or cited evidence.
reason.title: Reason

source_node.description: Completed node_id: run requires build; optimize accepts build/run/optimize; diagnose/crosscheck/video/finish require a valid evaluated run or optimize node. Never an artifact ID.
source_node.title: Source Node

variables.description: optimize only, required: variables[path] = [lower_bound, upper_bound], a continuous interval, NOT two requested samples. Bounds must be within the authorized space and include the starting value.
variables.title: Variables

message.content: I'll start by constructing a candidate from the frozen baseline. This build costs zero solver attempts, so I can inspect what the template does before spending a backend solve.
message.reasoning_content:
Let me start by inspecting the route to get the full overview, though it's already in context. Actually the overview is already present. Let me think about the task.

Task: reach task, target [0.29, 0.035, 0.19], tolerance 0.01 m. Two segment development baseline. Baseline two_segment_development: near flexible_segment length 0.16, far flexible_segment length 0.12, plus guide, connector, payload. Tendons 6, actuators 6.

Space: control/feedback_gain [2,8], discretization/cells/far [2,6], discretization/cells/near [2,6], parameters: components/near/interpolation choice (step,linear), components/near/length_m [0.14,0.2], components/far/sections/0/section/parameters/inner_radius_m [0.002,0.006] when kind=tube. Templates: tube_distal.

Authorized combinations: family_mujoco and matlab_spatial, both executable.

Plan: build with a combination, apply template tube_distal maybe, then run to evaluate. Then optimize on some variables.

I should start with build. Let me pick combination family_mujoco. Should I apply changes? The build constructs and validates only. Then run evaluates. Let's build the baseline (with maybe template tube_distal to enable the inner_radius parameter) and then optimize.

Actually let me think: we have 4 backend solves. max_trials 3. We want to minimize position error.

Step 1: build a candidate (zero solves). Then run (1 solve). Then optimize maybe with max_trials=3 on key variables (2 variables? variables allow any number of paths, each with bounds). Optimize consumes up to max_trials charged attempts.

Budget: 4 backend solves. If we do 1 run + 3 optimize trials = 4 solves. Then no crosscheck. Alternatively skip the initial run and go straight optimize with source_node = build, max_trials 3, then use remaining solve for run at best? Hmm.

Better plan: build (0 solves) with template tube_distal applied, then optimize from the build node with variables (e.g., near length and feedback gain) with max_trials=3 → 3 solves. Then use remaining 1 solve for crosscheck on alternative backend (matlab_spatial) for independent review. That uses 4 solves total. Then finish.

Actually crosscheck requires a valid run/optimize source node and authorized alternative backend combination. Good.

But careful: optimize with build source—does it count as build then evaluate candidates. Yes.

Let me first build. Which combination? family_mujoco. The build with changes: maybe apply template "tube_distal" and set components/near/interpolation to "linear".

Hmm, but applying tube_distal template might change far segment section kind to tube, enabling inner_radius parameter. That's a design choice. The target reach: 0.29, 0.035, 0.19 relative to mount at [0,0,0.15]. So displacement from mount ~ (0.29, 0.035, 0.04). Distance ~0.2938. Total arm length baseline = 0.16+0.12 = 0.28 (plus connector). Reach 0.294 > 0.28 straight, requires bending to be reachable... actually straight reach max is 0.28+connector maybe. Hmm, target distance 0.294 which exceeds 0.28, so a fully straight arm might not reach unless connector adds length. Actually bending doesn't increase reach. So target may be slightly out of reach; maximize straightness. Hmm but near length can go to 0.2, giving 0.32 total. So increasing near length helps reach.

Wait, but is the mounting at [0,0,0.15] and the arm extends upward in z? Target z=0.19, only 0.04 above mount. And x=0.29 forward. So arm must bend to horizontal-ish direction. With 2 segments, one bends.

Let's just build and run.

Let's do build first: node_id "build1", action build, combination family_mujoco, changes: {"template":"tube_distal", "components/near/interpolation":"linear"}? Hmm, the changes key for template is "template". Let me include template and maybe nothing else.

Actually minimal approach: build the baseline unchanged to see baseline behavior. Then optimize. But template tube_distal may be needed to expose inner_radius. Not necessary.

Let me do build with no changes (baseline) — safe. Then run to see baseline error.

Actually let's be efficient with solves. 4 solves: run baseline (1), then optimize 3 trials. Then finish. Or build with template then optimize 3, crosscheck 1.

I'll go: build baseline with template tube_distal applied (to allow richer optimization later and it's a declared option), then run... hmm.

Let me just start: build.

I'll choose changes: {"template": "tube_distal"}. Risk: template might alter geometry unexpectedly. Alternatively no changes.

I think safer to build with the template applied because the space lists templates ["tube_distal"] as an option, and inner_radius param only valid when far section kind is tube. But changing far to tube may change stiffness. Let's build with template and see the built candidate description in the result.

Let me do it. Provide evidence citation? "After the first action, cite at least one previous route node result reference." This is the first action, so no evidence needed.

Let me call route.advance build.

Actually the instructions say: "Call route.inspect and evidence.read in separate turns, never together." and "Use English for every explanation." Let's proceed with build.

I'll only call one tool per response. So build first.
